finding.claim: Cached verification results for tokens that have `exp` or `nbf` but no numeric `iat` ignore those claims. The result is served from cache for up to cacheTTL (default 600s) after the token expires. A cached token also keeps passing even though its `nbf` time check was never recorded.
finding.source: A validly signed token with `exp` but no numeric `iat`, such as one issued by a third-party IdP or with noTimestamp. It is presented repeatedly to a verifier with caching enabled. The cache option is on by default in many setups.
finding.sink: A cache hit returns the payload as valid from `verify()` (src/verifier.js:364-377) without re-running exp/nbf validation.

trace.note: hasIat = typeof payload.iat === 'number'; false when the token has no iat
The block that records nbf (min) and exp (max) runs only if hasIat, so cacheValue[1] and cacheValue[2] stay 0
cacheValue[2] === 0, so max falls back to clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 600000 ms), regardless of the token's exp
On the next call, min === 0 and now <= max, so the cache hit returns the payload even though exp has passed

finding.guards_checked: The expiry check in verifyToken (src/verifier.js:304-323) runs only on a cache miss. The cache hit path at lines 363-379 does not recheck exp. The maxTTL cap bounds the overshoot to cacheTTL but does not remove it. Setting the cache size to 0 avoids the problem. I did not execute this.

finding.claim: A verifier created with a falsy key and an explicit algorithms list accepts unsigned tokens with an empty signature segment. An empty-string key can come from an unset environment variable. A token with a forged payload is then accepted as long as its header `alg` is in the allowed list.
finding.source: An attacker-crafted token of the form base64url(header).base64url(payload). with an empty signature. Its header alg is an algorithm in the configured list, such as HS256. The precondition is a verifier created with key '' (a missing env secret) and algorithms: ['HS256'].
finding.sink: verifyToken returns without error, and verify() returns the attacker-chosen payload as authenticated claims.

trace.note: typeof '' is 'string', so the key option validation passes
`key &&` is falsy, so key detection and prepareKeyOrSecret are skipped and the key stays ''
With !hasKey and an empty signature, neither the missingSignature branch nor the missingKey branch is taken
The alg check passes because alg is in allowedAlgorithms, and the signature check is skipped at line 169 because signature is ''

finding.guards_checked: The key option type check accepts ''. There is no empty-key guard on the sync path; the empty-key check in prepareKeyOrSecret (line 38) is never reached. The decoder (src/decoder.js:41) allows an empty signature segment. This is a fail-open on misconfiguration, so exploitability depends on the key actually being empty. I did not execute this.
